page: Microsoft Azure F64s_v2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FSv2 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The server provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is provisioned with 524 GB of capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in memory bandwidth and extended CPU instructions. Uncached large-block memory read-only bandwidth reaches 208.5 GB/sec, and write bandwidth is measured at 91.43 GB/sec, both falling into the top 25% tier. The Passmark CPU extended instructions test also registers a strong score of 54,210.67. Other compute metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores, align with average mid-tier performance. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with text generation for a 70B model performing poorly at 2.4 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F64s_v2 offers a high density of compute resources relative to memory, making it a viable option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. The hardware profile is suited for batch processing, web serving, compilation tasks, and medium-sized database operations. It is also appropriate for workloads leveraging vector extensions due to its support for AVX and AVX-512 instructions.
